summary: Recent changes to the image decoding section of Firefox involved a series of updates aimed at enhancing security and performance. One significant improvement is the unification of how promises (a way to handle actions that take time, like loading images) are managed, making the process more efficient and reliable. Additionally, there are new restrictions on which image types can be loaded in certain contexts, specifically allowing only page icons and remote images to ensure safety and integrity when displaying images. Most notably, these changes help to **strengthen the browser's security by ensuring that responses from service workers (background scripts that help manage network requests) are properly handled**, reducing the risk of potential vulnerabilities when dealing with images from different origins. These updates represent a concerted effort to bolster Firefox's capabilities in handling images while maintaining user safety.
